prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: ফসল মৌসুমভিত্তিক বপন, কর্তন ও ফলন সূচি (language bn).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ফসল" · longest unbreakable word 69px · one-line width 149px
  col 2: header "বপন" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 263px
  col 3: header "কাটা" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 239px
  col 4: header "ফলন (টন/হেক্টর)" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 108px
  col 5: header "মন্তব্য" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 1035px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A crop-by-crop season reference: compare when each crop is sown and harvested, what it yields, and any notes.","reading":"Primarily row-wise: fix the crop in col 1, read cols 2–3 as one sowing-to-harvest window, then col 4 yield and col 5 caveat; secondarily scan down the date columns to compare seasons.","groups":["col 1 is the row anchor","cols 2–3 are a paired timing unit and must stay adjacent","col 4 is the quantitative outcome","col 5 is free-text commentary attached to the whole row"],"keep_intact":["crop names in col 1","month/season names and date ranges in cols 2–3","yield numbers and the টন/হেক্টর unit in col 4","row identity"],"may_wrap":["date ranges at spaces and em dashes","the yield header between ফলন and (টন/হেক্টর)","parenthetical crop qualifiers","comments in col 5, which must wrap extensively"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[90,67,65,63,74],"idea":"All five columns fit the phone by protecting crop names and the yield unit, while date words split and comments wrap in a very narrow well (359px total)."},{"name":"B","widths":[90,87,89,63,170],"idea":"Give the four data columns their no-split widths and a 149px comment well, accepting horizontal scroll mainly to read notes (499px total)."},{"name":"C","widths":[90,66,64,63,130],"idea":"Protect the row anchor, yield unit and a readable 109px notes well, squeeze the sowing/harvest pair, and accept a short horizontal scroll (413px total)."}]}
